result.summary:
Scope test: YES, application-executable surface present (Runner's new :audit_event_ordering verification method, real scenario execution against a running Letflow instance) -- full TEST-DESIGNER procedure applies, not the docs-only/config-only shortcut.

Reviewed test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs (897 lines, ELIXIR-DEV's Step 2a artifact, already REVIEWER-passed for idiom at Step 2d) against all 6 of REQ-207's acceptance criteria individually:

AC1 (production-order-above-threshold, all 4 expected outcomes verified): ADEQUATE as written. All 4 outcome_results asserted individually (eo1 task_assigned with observed.assignee_ref == 'role-controller' as the load-bearing routing evidence per design section 3.1, not just outcome==:pass; eo2/eo3/eo4 each individually asserted :pass). No gap found.

AC2 (supplier-quality-deviation-critical, EO-001 real timestamp ordering + sub-process spawn): ADEQUATE as written. Ordering claim goes beyond eo_ordering.outcome==:pass -- destructures the real observed first_ts/second_ts and independently re-derives DateTime.compare(first_ts, second_ts)==:lt (lines 639-642), a genuine second check on top of Runner's own verdict. Sub-process spawn verified via a real, directly-queried InstanceProjection row (find_child_by_parent_instance_id/2, OQ-2's resolution), asserting child != nil and child.status == :active, then goes further and drives the child to completion and re-verifies the parent cascades to :completed. No gap found.

AC3 (supplier-quality-deviation-false-positive, terminal node verified as end-false-positive SPECIFICALLY): GAP FOUND AND FIXED. The pre-existing test relied solely on the severity-classification task's TASK_COMPLETED event payload showing activated_nodes==[] as evidence of reaching end-false-positive. Verified by reading lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:373-379 (dispatch_end/3) and grepping every event_type append site under lib/letflow/: activated_nodes==[] is produced identically for EVERY terminal END node in this codebase (the token is unconditionally dropped on END arrival before any payload records which END node it was), and no persisted event anywhere carries the literal target-node id -- a real, confirmed platform gap, not a test-writing oversight. This means the pre-existing assertion could not actually distinguish 'reached end-false-positive' from a hypothetical bug that misrouted the false_positive==true edge to end-closed instead -- both produce activated_nodes==[] identically. Fixed by adding a structural cross-check against the seeded @simple_supplier_deviation_graph's own edge data (the real ground truth for which node a given edge/condition targets, since it's the actual definition instances ran against): asserts the false_positive==true edge's target is literally 'end-false-positive', refutes it being 'end-closed'. Verified non-vacuous by two mutations this session, both reverted: (1) flipping the seeded graph's own e3 edge target to 'end-closed' caused a real graph_validation_failed/isolated_node error at test setup (the process definition itself became invalid -- independently confirms the graph shape is load-bearing); (2) leaving the graph correct and flipping the test's own expected value instead produced a direct, isolated assertion failure quoting the real observed target. mix test test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs returned to 4/4 passed after both reverts.

AC4 (entity-list-filter-and-page, disposition determined by a re-runnable check): ADEQUATE as written. Confirmed the 3 signals (router.ex content, requirements.yaml title regex, entities.ex/entity_query.ex existence) are run live via File.read!/Regex.match?/File.exists? against real files at test-run time, not hardcoded booleans -- would flip if any underlying fact changed. No gap found.

AC5 (report states closed disposition for all 4 scenarios): confirmed by direct read of test/reports/req207-vortex-scenario-findings.yaml -- all 4 scenario ids present, each with a disposition field (EXECUTED x3, BLOCKED_ON_DEPENDENCY x1), no gaps. Not independently ExUnit-tested (a static YAML report's content is a build-artifact-review concern, same disposition REQ-205's own spec gave its report format -- see test/specs/REQ-205.md precedent).

AC6 (mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass): re-run this session (quoted below), not merely inherited from ELIXIR-DEV's prior claim.

Isolation/fixture hygiene checked: unique tenant slug per test via Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug('req207') inside the shared setup block (runs per-test, not setup_all); grepped for DateTime.utc_now/:rand/System.os_time -- none found, no wall-clock/unseeded-randomness dependency; async:false is required only for Sandbox.mode(:auto) (real Postgres), each test provisions/tears down its own schema independently via setup/on_exit, no cross-test ordering dependency; no hardcoded secrets/connection strings.
